title: Nondeterministic interval guess
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with oracle, let $x$ be an input, and let $B$ be a register bound. Choose distinct registers $g,nr$ and states $test,ch,more,ex,rej$. Suppose the deterministic instruction at $test$ compares $g$ with $nr$, branching to $rej$ when they are equal and to $ch$ otherwise; at $ch$ the program may choose $ex$ or $more$; at $more$ it increments $g$ and returns to $test$; and at $rej$ it halts with answer false. Let $Q$ be a predicate on natural numbers, and let $v$ be an initial register assignment with every register at most $B$ and $v(g)\le v(nr)$. If, for every $j$ with $v(g)\le j<v(nr)$, the configuration at $ex$ with $g$ set to $j$ and all other registers unchanged terminates within the register bound and accepts exactly when $Q(j)$ holds, then the configuration at $test$ with assignment $v$ terminates within that bound and accepts exactly when some $j$ in that interval satisfies $Q(j)$.
